_comment: RF02 reproduction input — DynamicAllowList at max_grants=2 holding one live grant; two independent staging tokens reserve the SAME key (name+addr+quals). Headroom exists for the shared key (live 1 + 1 new key = 2, at capacity), so a refusal can only come from counting the staged key once per token: current capacity accounting totals live + staged distinct keys and refuses the second token's reservation even though committing it merges into a single live entry. A DISTINCT third key under the same capacity stays denied — the overflow path this case must not weaken. Executed verbatim by bench target m4_allowlist's `rf02` block; the regression test lands in RF02's PR.

observed_before_fix.source: m4_allowlist rf02 block, run-2026-11-17-01 rerun, parent+candidate identical

expected_after_fix.note: commit:s1 merges the shared key once; drop:s2 removes only s2's hold. Distinct-key overflow under the same capacity must still fail.

related_cases_for_rf02_tests: drop s2 then commit s1 (reverse order)
commit s1 then commit s2 (reverse order — second commit is a no-op on the same key)
staged update of the EXISTING live key under full capacity
staged reservation of a DISTINCT key under full capacity — must stay denied
same addr, different name — distinct key, distinct capacity
TTL/scope update semantics unchanged; uncommitted reservations invisible to is_allowed/snapshot_json/export_to
